definition.description: For a single word: short English definition of this sense (under 12 words). Omit for phrases.

expression.description: Report ONLY for a FIXED multi-word unit the word belongs to — one Spanish says as a chunk, where swapping a component for a near-synonym gives something nobody says ("prestar atención", never "dar atención"): an idiom or fixed phrase, a discourse marker ("sin embargo", "en realidad"), a fixed compound noun ("sala de estar"), or a fixed quantity or degree expression ("un sinfín de"). Fixedness decides, not transparency: report the unit even when its word-for-word English is already natural. Do NOT report free combinations or verb+preposition government (e.g. "soñar con"), and do NOT report open-slot frames whose slots hold free content ("tanto la cocina como la tarta" instantiates tanto…como — put the frame in note instead). The whole expression, copied EXACTLY as it appears in the sentence — identical words, accents, and conjugation (do NOT normalize to the infinitive or dictionary form). Omit for an ordinary standalone word.

expressionMeaning.description: English meaning of that expression as used here, SUBSTITUTABLE for exactly the words of the expression — never absorbing tense, subject, or a verb that follows it ("volver a" = "to … again", never "to laugh again"). The single best rendering — never two alternatives joined by " / " or a restating comma. Omit unless expression is reported.

formNote.description: How the word relates to its dictionary form, very short: tense/mood + person for conjugated verbs ("imperfect, 3rd person singular"), "plural"/"feminine" for inflected nouns/adjectives. Omit if it IS the dictionary form or a phrase.

lemma.description: Dictionary form (infinitive for verbs, masculine singular for nouns/adjectives). For a verb standing without its pronoun, the PLAIN infinitive, never the reflexive (detuvo → detener, not detenerse), unless the verb exists only pronominally (quejarse). A past participle used as an adjective takes the INFINITIVE when it only names the verb's action (colgada → colgar, cerrada → cerrar); it keeps its own masculine singular ONLY when it has a settled sense of its own (educado "polite", parecido "similar", detenido "careful"). Omit if identical or a phrase.

note.description: One short note ONLY when genuinely helpful: idiom meaning, false friend, register. Usually omit.

partOfSpeech.description: One lowercase word (noun, verb, adjective…). Omit for phrases.

senses.description: At most two OTHER common senses of this word a learner would meet in modern prose, each 1-4 words and DISTINCT from the translation already given. Return an EMPTY ARRAY when there is nothing to add — phrases, proper names, and words with essentially one sense. Never archaic, technical, or rare dictionary tails — only senses worth recognizing on the next page.

translation.description: English translation as used in the sentence. Concise: 1-4 words for a word; for a phrase, fluent English that covers ALL of it, dropping none of its words. The single best rendering — never two alternatives joined by " / " or a restating comma.
